elements.text: Meerkats in Africa live in groups called mobs. The meerkats in a mob look out for each other and work together as a team. This helps meerkats stay safe from danger, such as other animals.
Meerkats take turns being the "lookout," for example. The lookout climbs to a high place. It stands on its back legs to see better. If it spots any trouble, the lookout will bark to warn the others.
All the meerkats watch over the babies, too. They take turns babysitting! Together, they make sure that no other animals can harm the little ones.

The leaf trap fills up with a kind of juice. It turns the insect into a healthy soup that the plant soaks up. When the plant is ready for another meal, it opens its leaves again.

Workers go out and hunt for food. They build the hive, protect it, and keep it clean. They also take care of the queen's babies. The workers are always female bees.
The male bees are called drones. Their only job is to mate with the queen so she can lay eggs.

Climbers also have to worry about large cracks in the ice called crevasses. Some crevasses on Everest are so deep, climbers can fall into them.
The air is another problem. The higher people climb, the thinner the air is. So, it becomes harder to breathe. But some amazing climbers still make it all the way to the top!

header.text: Here are some examples:

sentences.text: Megan was glum when her best friend moved away.
You can guess that glum means "sad."
He said sorry, but I was still irate.
You can guess that irate means "angry."
Mr. Lee keeps his home tidy and clean.
You can guess that tidy means "neat."
Be cautious! Move slowly and watch your step.
You can guess that cautious means "careful."
